rules: Rust edition 2021. No unsafe code. Use only the dependencies in the crate manifest (forge-core, forge-work, chrono, serde_json, sha2, tokio, tokio-postgres, uuid).
The public surface is synchronous. Never expose tokio or tokio-postgres types in public signatures; they stay inside PgSession.

All SQL goes through PgSession/Tx helpers (call_* for the SQL-function surfaces; query_rows/execute_count for the work-store adapters' raw SQL). Never build SQL strings beyond the literal statements pinned in the card. Function names, argument order and result types come from the card exactly.
Leases are explicit values: nothing is cleaned up by Drop, and every fallible operation returns Result<_, AdapterError>.
Every public item carries a /// doc comment.
Unit tests go in a #[cfg(test)] mod tests at the bottom of the same file and test pure logic only - never a live database.
No binary, no main function, no environment access anywhere in this crate.
One file is one generation unit: at most ~90 lines. If a design needs more, it belongs in two cards (split into submodules at the design level) - never write a file longer than ~110 lines.
Work-adapter helpers that touch tokio_postgres::Row are pub(crate) only; the public adapter surface is PgWorkStore and the forge-work port traits.
